_doc: Non-CSFA CA charter school muni conduit enumeration — CMFA, CSCDA, CalPFA, PCSD (Blueprint Futures), CCSA-FA. Built to expand charter_universe_v2.json beyond the CSFA-dominated 23-obligor base.
_methodology: Per-conduit primary-source enumeration: (a) CMFA annual report FY24 (audited financial statement 6/30/24) — Financing Approvals schedule listing all initial+final resolutions for FY24; (b) CMFA news/press archive — search of /charter/+/academy/ tagged announcements 2018-2024; (c) CSCDA resources page (transactions + audit PDFs identified); (d) CalPFA Approved Transactions FY24/25 PDF (CalPFA Authorized_Bonds_7.2024-6.2025.pdf); (e) PCSD/Blueprint Futures website (school-partners enumeration of logo grid, plus Projects featured-page); (f) CCSA Financing Authority website unreachable (ECONNREFUSED). All transaction-level data cited to source URL. Where conduit FY-report PDFs were not text-extractable in agent context (CSFA 2024 Appendix A image-only schedule, CalPFA FS image-scan), this is noted as DATA_GAP_PDF_NOT_PARSEABLE.
_critical_finding_zero_2024_cmfa_cscda_c: Per CSFA's own 2024 Conduit Financing Program Report (https://www.treasurer.ca.gov/csfa/financings/conduit/2024.pdf): 'Of the 19 tax-exempt charter school bonds and notes issued in California in 2024 and reported on EMMA, CSFA issued 13 (~68%), CEDA issued 4 (~21%), IBank issued 2 (~11%).' THIS MEANS CMFA, CSCDA, AND CalPFA HAD ZERO 2024 CHARTER SCHOOL CONDUIT ISSUANCE PER CSFA SELF-DISCLOSURE. The 'other non-CSFA conduits' in 2024 were CEDA (California Enterprise Development Authority — Wonderful Foundation deal) and IBank (CA Infrastructure & Economic Development Bank — Magnolia Public Schools refunding). This means: (1) v2 universe's `cmfa_intercept_or_other` and `calpfa_other` enum values currently apply ONLY to PRE-2024 historical issuances; (2) need to add CEDA and IBank as conduit_issuer enums to v3 universe.

pcsd_lessees._observation_critical: PCSD rebranded to Blueprint Futures (https://blueprintfutures.org/, formerly https://www.pacificcharter.org/). PCSD is NOT a bond conduit issuer — it is a non-profit DEVELOPER that owns charter school real estate and leases to charter operators. The bond exposure is through PCSD-related financing vehicles (e.g. Local Initiatives Support Corp / Charter School Lending pools, and PCSD's own audited financial statement). Total portfolio per Blueprint website: '143 School Facilities Built or Renovated' across CA, WA, TX, CO since 2004. 57,546 total seats. $1.44B invested.

pcsd_lessees.v2_universe_overlap: MASSIVE — Aspire, Alliance, Bright Star, Camino Nuevo, Ednovate, Equitas, Green Dot, KIPP NorCal, Lighthouse, PUC, Summit, Caliber are ALL both in v2 universe AND Blueprint partners. This means: (1) v2 obligors that have CSFA-issued operator bonds ALSO have facility-lease exposure to PCSD/Blueprint as landlord; (2) PCSD-pool credit risk is largely a function of the SAME operator pool already in v2. (3) Net-new obligors NOT in v2 from PCSD pool: ~30 additional CA charters (Aveson, Bloom, Catalyst, Center for World Languages, Clovis Global, Education for Change, El Sol, Elevate Collegiate, Environmental Charter Schools, Envision, Fenton, Gabriella, Golden Charter Academy, Navigator, OCEAA, Pasadena Rosebud, Ross Valley, STEM Prep, Voices, YPICS, Yuming, Alma Fuerte, Alpha, BayTech, CWC LA West Valley, Excel Academy, Pinnacles, Royal, Thrive, UP Excellence).
pcsd_lessees._critical_finding_pool_structure: The PCSD/Blueprint pool structure (per masking_mechanisms.json pcsd_facility_credit entry) masks SINGLE-CHARTER operator distress — but the framework can still extract signal from individual operators (charter renewal denials, 990 deterioration, authorizer actions). The PCSD-pool muni bond holders (LISC charter pool, PCSD direct facility bond) get diversification benefit only if the operators are uncorrelated. The fact that ALL CA-relevant PCSD partners are LAUSD/OUSD/Bay Area authorizer-concentrated means CORRELATED authorizer risk likely.
pcsd_lessees._data_gap: PCSD/Blueprint does NOT publicly publish (a) Form 990 Schedule R lessee-by-lessee rent-payment data, (b) per-facility bond/financing structure (which lessees back which bond), (c) which schools are current lessees vs former, (d) whether v2 obligors like Aspire/Alliance/Camino-Nuevo lease facilities directly OR only via construction-services. The 990 itself (EIN 20-0696786) would need direct download from IRS / ProPublica raw XML to extract Schedule R related-org details. Time-boxed: not pulled this pass.

ccsa_fa._observation: ccsafinancingauthority.com returns CONNECTION_REFUSED in agent context. Public-web search for 'CCSA Financing Authority' returns minimal hits. Per LISC + NCSRC: California Charter Schools Association operates the California Charter Building Fund (CCBF) — a first-loss reserve / credit-enhancement grant fund, NOT a conduit bond issuer. CCBF lends ~1% below conventional risk-adjusted pricing, with grant reserves to pay defaulted debt service. This is a credit-enhancement layer behind OTHER conduits' bonds (CSFA, CMFA), not a standalone bond issuer.
ccsa_fa._critical_finding_structure_reclassifica: v2 universe's 'ccsa_jpa_pool' structure_class enum value appears to be a MISCLASSIFICATION — there is no public evidence of a CCSA-administered joint powers authority issuing standalone charter pool bonds. The CCSA's role is credit-enhancement (CCBF grant reserve) layered on bonds issued by CSFA/other conduits. v3 should likely REPLACE 'ccsa_jpa_pool' with 'csfa_or_other_with_ccsa_credit_enhancement' as a sub-class, OR drop it if no obligor in universe actually uses CCBF-backed debt.
ccsa_fa._data_gap: CCSA Financing Authority website inaccessible. Annual report not retrieved. If a CCSA-FA bond pool genuinely exists separately from CCBF grant fund, this pass did not surface it. Recommend: search EMMA for 'California Charter Schools Association' issuer name; check IRS EIN-lookup for CCSA Financing Authority entity registration.

_summary.v2_coverage_expansion_estimate: v2 had 23 obligors with verifiable bonds (~20% CA charter universe). Adding the 10 CMFA charter operators + ~30 PCSD-only-lessee obligors (those not already in v2) brings universe to ~63 obligors. Estimated coverage now ~50-55% of CA charter universe — short of the 70-80% target. Gap is in (a) bank-purchased private placement charter debt (no SEC disclosure), (b) smaller stand-alone charters with no public bond debt, (c) CSCDA pre-2018 issuances not surfaced by news search.

_critical_findings_for_v3_universe_build: FINDING #1: CMFA/CSCDA/CalPFA had ZERO 2024 charter school issuance per CSFA's own 2024 Conduit Financing Program Report. The non-CSFA 2024 conduits were CEDA (4 deals) and IBank (2 deals). v3 universe MUST add structure_class values 'ceda_intercept_or_other' and 'ibank_intercept_or_other'. Known deals: Wonderful Foundation (CEDA portion), Magnolia Public Schools (IBank refi portion).

FINDING #2: TVLC (Tri-Valley Learning Corporation) is a CONFIRMED CA charter facility bond DEFAULT, with both CMFA and CSCDA exposure. v3 should add as historical_distress_reference. This is high-value training data for honesty-alpha framework (defaulted charters give us ground-truth for what 'liar detection' would have caught pre-default).

FINDING #3: The 'ccsa_jpa_pool' structure_class in v2 appears to be a misclassification. CCSA's California Charter Building Fund (CCBF) is a credit-enhancement grant reserve, not a JPA bond pool. v3 should drop or restructure this enum.

FINDING #4: PCSD/Blueprint Futures pool has ~43 CA charter operator lessees, MOST OF WHICH OVERLAP with v2 obligors (Aspire, Alliance, Bright Star, Camino Nuevo, Caliber, Ednovate, Equitas, Green Dot, KIPP NorCal, Lighthouse, PUC, Summit). This means the PCSD-pool credit risk is largely COVARIATE with v2 operator-credit risk. The masking benefit of pool-level diversification is weaker than headline ~43-name pool size suggests, given authorizer concentration (LAUSD, OUSD).

FINDING #5: CMFA charter deals use a notable structural variation — Julian Charter School borrowed via 'SDORI Charter School Properties, LLC', a single-purpose facility LLC. This is the 'cmfa_llc_facility_vehicle' subclass — operator credit fully exposed because the LLC has no LCFF apportionment of its own. Different from a direct-charter CMFA borrower like John Adams Academy. v3 should distinguish these subclasses.

FINDING #6: PCSD owns property in ~30 CA charter operators that are NOT in v2 universe (Alma Fuerte, Alpha, Bloom, Catalyst, Center for World Languages, Clovis Global, etc.). These operators may have NO direct muni bond exposure (PCSD is the bondholder via its own facility bonds), making them invisible to EMMA-based universe construction. To bring these into v3 requires pulling PCSD's own bond stack.
